title: Failure Scenarios and Degraded Operations
description: The TDPO learns to manage single and compound failures in DP operations, assess degraded capability, and make correct decisions about continuing or aborting operations. Professional standard means the TDPO never freezes, always assesses remaining capability before deciding, and communicates clearly and immediately. No failure scenario is announced in advance.

tasks.title: Single Thruster Failure Near Structure
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP at operating radius of virtual structure. Moderate conditions settled. DPO will trigger a single thruster failure at an unannounced time during the hold.
tasks.execute: When the thruster failure occurs, hold position with remaining thrusters. Identify the faulted thruster. Assess new worst case failure. Assess remaining capability for current conditions. Decide whether to maintain position or increase standoff distance. Communicate your decision and reasoning to DPO as if communicating to OIM.
professional_standard: Position maintained within double the normal footprint
Correct new worst case failure identified
Correct capability assessment for current conditions

Notes

debrief_questions: How did your worst case failure change when one thruster was lost — and why does that matter?
Was your decision to hold position or increase standoff correct given remaining capability and conditions?
What would the ASOG say about continuing operations with this degraded thruster complement?
What is your new abort threshold with reduced thrusters — at what environmental condition would you now go off DP?

variants.title: Single Thruster Failure in Heavy Weather
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same failure in heavier conditions. The margin between capable and incapable is much narrower. Your decision to hold or depart will be harder to justify either way.

variants.title: Critical Thruster Failure
variants.note_to_tdpo: Your DPO will select the most operationally critical thruster to fail for your vessel configuration. This may mean an immediate departure decision is the only safe choice.

tasks.title: Power Failure Response
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP. DPO will trigger a generator dropout on one bus without warning. Know your vessel power configuration — which thrusters are on which bus — before this drill.
tasks.execute: When the generator dropout occurs, observe which thrusters lose power. Observe auto load shedding. Assess remaining propulsion capability. Prevent blackout. Either hold position or initiate controlled departure. Communicate to DPO as OIM.
professional_standard: Correct identification of thrusters lost on faulted bus
Auto load shedding observed and understood

Notes

debrief_questions: Which thrusters lost power and does the bus configuration of your vessel explain why those ones specifically?
What is the role of blackout prevention in this scenario — what would happen without it?
Why does the bus tie position matter so much in a power failure scenario?
What is the worst case failure for this vessel and how does this event relate to it — was this the WCF or something different?

variants.title: Power Failure Near Structure
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same power failure at 90m from structure. Your decision window is shorter and the consequences of the wrong decision are higher. Decide fast and communicate clearly.

tasks.title: Compound Failure — Reference Loss During Approach
tasks.setup: Begin an active approach to virtual structure from 500m. DPO will trigger reference loss at an unannounced point during the approach — inside the 500m zone.
tasks.execute: Continue the approach normally. When reference loss occurs inside the 500m zone, make an immediate decision — continue approach on remaining references or abort. If continuing, hold position and reassess. If aborting, execute a controlled departure. There is no correct answer predetermined — your decision must be reasoned and clearly communicated.
professional_standard: Correct minimum reference assessment at moment of failure

variants.title: Compound Failure — Reference Loss Plus Environmental Increase
variants.note_to_tdpo: Reference loss and wind increase occur simultaneously during the approach. Two problems at once. Prioritise the higher risk issue first — which is it?

tasks.title: Worst Case Failure Exercise
tasks.setup: Vessel on DP at operating radius of virtual structure. Moderate to heavy conditions. Before starting, state to your DPO what you understand to be the vessels defined worst case failure. DPO will then trigger it without further warning during the hold.
tasks.execute: When the WCF is triggered, observe the full system response — position excursion, alarm sequence, thruster redistribution. Record the excursion distance. Assess whether the excursion would be within safe limits for a notional subsea operation with divers at 50m depth. Make a safety assessment and communicate it clearly.
professional_standard: Full alarm sequence observed and recorded
Correct safety assessment for subsea operation context

variants.title: WCF in Heavy Weather
variants.note_to_tdpo: Same WCF in significantly heavier conditions. The excursion will be larger and recovery may not occur. Observe the full consequence and assess whether operations should ever be conducted in these conditions on this vessel.
